explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - MoonTV is a full-stack, server-rendered web application (Next.js 14 + App Router) that aggregates multiple video sources into a unified player/UI, provides a built-in admin panel (REST API under /src/app/api/admin/*), and persists user data (favorites, watch history) in Redis-style stores (Kvrocks/Redis/Upstash). It’s packaged as a Docker-ready monolith with PWA support.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level Docker + CI/CD: Dockerfile, .dockerignore, GitHub Actions workflow under .github/workflows/docker-image.yml  
   - Config & build: next.config.js, tsconfig.json, tailwind.config.ts, jest.config.js, lint/prettier configs  
   - Public/static: /public (icons, logo, robots.txt)  
   - App Router pages & API routes:  
     • /src/app/*.tsx (UI pages: home, search, detail, play, admin)  
     • /src/app/api/*/**/route.ts (REST endpoints for admin, auth, search, proxy, live, douban, etc.)  
   - Components: /src/components (reusable React components)  
   - Hooks: /src/hooks (e.g., useLongPress)  
   - Lib: /src/lib (db clients, auth, external-API wrappers, caching, utils)  
   - Middleware: src/middleware.ts (edge middleware for auth/redirects)  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Tech stack: Next.js 14, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, ArtPlayer, HLS.js  
   - Storage options: Kvrocks, Redis, Upstash (via env vars NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_TYPE, KVROCKS_URL, REDIS_URL, UPSTASH_URL/TOKEN)  
   - Deployment: Docker Compose (core + Kvrocks/Redis), Zeabur one-click  

4. Designing the system architecture diagram  
   a. Main components:  
      • Client (Browser/PWA)  
      • Next.js Server (Node.js container)  
      • Data stores (Kvrocks/Redis/Upstash)  
      • External APIs & services (Douban API or proxies, video/CDN endpoints)  
   b. Relationships & data flows:  
      1. Client → HTTP(S) → Next.js Server  
         ‑ UI page requests (SSR/SSG) and API calls (/api/*)  
      2. Next.js Server ↔ Data store  
         ‑ Reads/writes favorites, watch history, config cache  
      3. Next.js Server → External services  
         ‑ Douban data fetch, site-provided VOD APIs, ad-skipping logic, image proxies, HLS segment proxy  
      4. Client ← HLS.js/ArtPlayer ← (via Next.js proxy or direct CDN) video streams  
   c. Architectural patterns / design principles:  
      - Monolithic Node.js container with layered structure: Presentation (React+Tailwind), Business Logic (API routes + lib services), Data Access (db clients), Integration adapters (external API wrappers)  
      - API routes as serverless-style functions inside Next.js  
      - PWA caching (service worker) for offline/installation  
      - Edge middleware for auth and routing  
      - Config driven by environment variables injected at container runtime  
   d. Key technologies/frameworks:  
      - Next.js 14 App Router & Server Actions  
      - React + Tailwind CSS  
      - Docker (core + Kvrocks/Redis containers)  
      - Redis-compatible stores (Kvrocks, Upstash)  
      - ArtPlayer & HLS.js for video playback  
      - Jest + ESLint + Prettier for code quality  

5. Tailoring diagram for a full-stack web application  
   - Draw separate horizontal layers:  
     1. Presentation Layer (Browser/PWA)  
     2. Application Layer (Next.js Node.js process)  
     3. Data Layer (Redis-compatible store)  
     4. Integration Layer (External APIs & Video/CDN)  
   - Emphasize the clear boundary between:  
     • UI pages (/src/app/*.tsx + components)  
     • API layer (/src/app/api/*)  
     • Data access (/src/lib/db*.ts)  
     • External connectors (/src/lib/douban.client.ts, proxy routes)  

6. Elements to include in the diagram  
   - Clear labels on each component (e.g., “Next.js App Container”, “Kvrocks Store”, “Douban Proxy API”)  
   - Directional arrows showing request/response flows (HTTP GET/POST, WebSocket if any)  
   - Color coding or distinct shapes:  
     • Blue rectangles for UI/client  
     • Green for application/server  
     • Orange cylinder for database  
     • Purple clouds for external services/CDN  

7. Additional guidelines  
   - Annotate environment-driven components (e.g., storage type selection)  
   - Show CI/CD pipeline block (GitHub Actions → Docker image → Zeabur/Vercel) if relevant  
   - Capture PWA service worker caching flow between client and CDN  

By following these steps—identifying layers, mapping data flows, labeling components, and applying color coding—you’ll produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that reflects MoonTV’s full-stack architecture, from user-facing React pages through Next.js API routes down to the Redis-compatible persistence layer and external video/CDN integrations.
</explanation>
